lines: Python runs your lines from top to bottom. Write price equals forty and tune ups equals twenty five, then print price times tune ups, and it prints one thousand. The equals sign means store this.
A list keeps many numbers under one name. For the list twenty, twenty five, thirty, sum gives seventy five and len counts three items. Seventy five over three gives the average: twenty five.
A for loop repeats the lines indented under it. Start with one thousand dollars, and three times, multiply by one point one. You get eleven hundred, twelve ten, then thirteen thirty one.

Now your savings. Each year, grow the balance by seven percent, then add twenty four hundred dollars. Thirty passes later, you have about two hundred twenty six thousand seven hundred dollars. Only seventy two thousand of it is your own money.
Put the rates in a list and loop over them, and one program tests four, seven and ten percent at once. Going from four to ten percent nearly triples what you end with.
A function, made with def, wraps steps you reuse, and return sends back the answer. An if lets code decide: if the NPV is more than zero, print build it.
For big data, finance teams use pandas. A DataFrame is a table in code. An Excel sheet stops at about one million rows; pandas can add up hundreds of millions in one line.
